manifest_row.title: Ambient locally finite mod-two relative chains for candidate regions
manifest_row.design_state: Root-authorized local ambient LF relative-chain helper; actual proof authored, ordinary native disposition and metadata adoption pending.
manifest_row.statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a locally compact Hausdorff space and $B\subseteq\Sigma$ closed. Use $\mathbb Z_2=\{0,1\}$ with addition modulo two. A chain in $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)$ is a formal sum of continuous singular $k$-simplex maps with mod-two coefficients such that every point of $\Sigma$ has a neighborhood meeting only finitely many nonzero simplex images. Put $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)=0$ for $k<0$. Let $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma;B)$ be the subgroup of these **ambient** chains whose simplex images are contained in $B$, and set
$$C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma,B):=C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)/C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma;B).$$
The face boundary, with all signs equal to plus in $\mathbb Z_2$, is well-defined and locally finite, preserves the $B$-supported subgroup, and induces $\bar\partial^2=0$ on this quotient. Define
$$H_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma,B):=\ker\bar\partial_k/\operatorname{im}\bar\partial_{k+1}.$$
For ambient locally finite chains $a,x$ with boundaries supported in $B$, the equality $[a]=[x]$ holds exactly when there is $r\in C_{k+1}^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)$ with $\partial r+a+x\in C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma;B)$. Changing representatives by quotient boundaries or $B$-supported chains preserves this criterion. Finite ordinary chains are allowed; on compact $\Sigma$ this is precisely the ordinary relative singular chain model.

Here is an explicit meaning of supplied fundamental-chain data. Let $Y\subseteq\Sigma$ be an embedded $n$-manifold with boundary, $n\ge1$. An **ambient locally finite mod-two fundamental chain for $Y$** is a chain $c\in C_n^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma)$ whose simplex maps land in $Y$, whose boundary maps land in $\partial Y$, and which satisfies the following local condition. For each $p\in Y\setminus\partial Y$, retain the finitely many simplices of $c$ whose images contain $p$, obtaining an ordinary finite chain $c_p$ in $Y$. Its class in $H_n(Y,Y\setminus\{p\};\mathbb Z_2)$ is the unique nonzero element. The boundary of $c_p$ avoids $p$, so this class is defined. The local group is $\mathbb Z_2$, without an orientation choice. These are explicit conditions on supplied chains, not an assertion that arbitrary nonproper embeddings push intrinsic locally finite chains into $\Sigma$.

A sufficient construction is as follows. Supply a pure $n$-dimensional ordered-vertex locally finite triangulation of $Y$, with boundary a subcomplex, whose realized simplex maps into $\Sigma$ form a locally finite family. Proper inclusion of a locally finite triangulated $Y$ into $\Sigma$ is sufficient for this ambient condition. Require that each interior codimension-one face has two incident top simplices and each boundary face has one. For every interior point $p$, supply a finite subcomplex neighborhood $N_p$ which is a compact $n$-manifold with boundary, with $p$ in its interior, such that the sum of its parametrized top simplices represents its compact mod-two relative fundamental class. A compact manifold ball or star with its verified relative fundamental chain supplies such a local certificate; no claim about an arbitrary triangulation's local stars is made. Then the sum of **all** top simplices, parametrized in the supplied vertex order, is an ambient locally finite fundamental chain for $Y$. For a supplied triangulated region whose boundary faces are divided into the $a$-faces, the $x$-faces and faces supported in $B$, this construction gives the displayed relative-chain criterion directly. No existence of a triangulation, a region, a chain certificate or an admissible candidate is asserted.

references.title: Allen Hatcher, Algebraic Topology, relative chains and manifold local homology
references.locator: The existing pinned relative-chain and local-homology suppliers are used below. The ambient locally finite quotient and the sufficient construction with supplied local certificates are proved locally; no new external full-text reading is claimed.

manifest_public_section.name: Definition
manifest_public_section.expected: Fix a smooth Lorentzian bulk spacetime $(M,g)$ and a supplied timelike conformal boundary. A **boundary Cauchy slice** is a smooth spacelike hypersurface of that boundary which every inextendible causal curve in the boundary meets exactly once. A **boundary region** $A$ is a relatively compact open subset of such a slice with smooth boundary $\partial A$. Fix a specified homology class $\mathcal H_A$ and a supplied class $\mathcal X_A$ (which may be empty) of smooth embedded codimension-two surfaces $X$, meaning $\dim X=\dim M-2$, with $\partial X=\partial A$. **Spacelike** means that the induced metric on $X$ is positive definite. Membership in $\mathcal H_A$ means that the model supplies an admissible bulk region $R_X$ whose relative boundary is $A\cup X$ on its chosen bulk Cauchy slice. The existence of any such surface is input data, not a consequence of this definition.
manifest_public_section.replacement:
Fix an integer $d\ge2$, a smooth time-oriented $(d+1)$-manifold with boundary $\overline M$, its interior $M$, and a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ on $M$ with signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. The model supplies a dimensionless smooth defining function $z:\overline M\to[0,\infty)$ with $z>0$ on $M$, $z=0$ and $dz\ne0$ on $\mathscr I:=\partial\overline M$, such that $\overline g:=z^2g$ extends smoothly to a nondegenerate metric on $\overline M$ whose induced metric $\gamma:=\overline g|_{T\mathscr I}$ is Lorentzian. Thus $\mathscr I$ is a timelike conformal boundary; its time orientation is fixed as model data.

The model supplies a time orientation on $(\overline M,\overline g)$ compatible with the chosen orientations on its interior and timelike boundary. A future-directed causal curve in $(\overline M,\overline g)$ or $(\mathscr I,\gamma)$ is a locally Lipschitz map $\eta:J\to\overline M$ or $\eta:J\to\mathscr I$, respectively, from a real interval, with a nonzero future-directed tangent almost everywhere and $\overline g(\dot\eta,\dot\eta)\le0$ or $\gamma(\dot\eta,\dot\eta)\le0$. Extensions are geometric: a regular increasing reparameterization is an order-preserving locally bi-Lipschitz homeomorphism $h:J\to J_0$ onto an interval. A curve is **inextendible** if there are no such $h$, a larger interval $\widetilde J$ containing $J_0$ as a proper subinterval, and a causal curve $\widetilde\eta:\widetilde J\to\overline M$ (or to $\mathscr I$ in the boundary case) with $\widetilde\eta\circ h=\eta$. Thus a parametrization on all of $\mathbb R$ does not by itself make a curve inextendible. A **boundary Cauchy slice** $\mathcal C_{\partial}$ is a smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface in $(\mathscr I,\gamma)$ whose inverse image under every inextendible boundary causal curve consists of exactly one parameter value. A **bulk Cauchy slice** for it is a smooth embedded spacelike $d$-dimensional hypersurface $\Sigma$ of $(\overline M,\overline g)$ with $\partial\Sigma=\mathcal C_{\partial}$ whose inverse image under every inextendible causal curve in $\overline M$ consists of exactly one parameter value. This is explicitly a boundary-inclusive convention: curves may meet or run along $\mathscr I$, and no ordinary Cauchy property for the AdS interior alone is imposed. Existence of these slices is supplied model data, not a theorem about every asymptotically AdS spacetime. For each candidate $X$, the model supplies such a slice $\Sigma_X$ containing $X$; one common slice is allowed.

A **boundary region** $A$ is a relatively compact open subset of $\mathcal C_{\partial}$ with smooth boundary $\partial A$; write $\overline A$ for its closure in $\mathcal C_{\partial}$. A candidate $X$ is a smooth embedded $(d-1)$-dimensional submanifold with boundary of $\overline M$, with $X\cap\mathscr I=\partial X=\partial A$, $X\setminus\partial X\subset M$, $X\subseteq\Sigma_X$, and positive-definite induced metric $\overline g|_{TX}$ (equivalently, $g|_{TX}$ is positive definite in the interior). Set $B_A:=\mathcal C_{\partial}\setminus A$, a closed subspace of $\Sigma_X$ since $\mathcal C_{\partial}=\partial\Sigma_X$ is closed and $A$ is open in it. Use the ambient locally finite mod-two relative chain model of [[lem-tgrx-locally-finite-relative-chain-model]]: $C_k^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma_X)$ consists of formal singular-simplex sums whose images are locally finite in $\Sigma_X$; quotient by its subgroup supported in $B_A$, and take the homology of the induced face boundary. The mod-two coefficients mean $1+1=0$. The model supplies a finite fundamental chain $a_X$ for the compact manifold with boundary $\overline A$ and an ambient locally finite fundamental chain $x$ for $X$, with boundaries supported in $\partial A$. Here fundamental means precisely the lemma's local condition: at every interior point of the represented manifold the finite point-local relative chain has the unique nonzero mod-two local homology class. These are supplied chain data; local finiteness is required in the ambient slice, and is not inferred by pushing an intrinsic chain through an arbitrary nonproper inclusion. Define $\mathcal H_A$ by $[x]=[a_X]$ in $H_{d-1}^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma_X,B_A;\mathbb Z_2)$. Equivalently, the model supplies $r_X\in C_d^{\mathrm{lf}}(\Sigma_X)$ with $\partial r_X+a_X+x$ supported in $B_A$; denote this relative chain by $R_X$. The lemma proves the quotient boundary is well-defined, squares to zero and gives exactly this equivalence. Finite chain witnesses remain allowed, and on a compact slice this is the ordinary finite relative homology model. When $R_X$ is represented by an ordinary bulk region, its supplied ambient locally finite fundamental chain is used. A proper compatible locally finite triangulation with the lemma's finite local fundamental-class certificates is a sufficient concrete construction by mod-two face cancellation, not a requirement on the full candidate class. The supplied class $\mathcal X_A$ (possibly empty) includes all this slice and chain data; no candidate, region, chain or triangulation existence theorem is asserted.

A named finite-regulator sequence for $X\in\mathcal X_A$ consists of labels $(\Lambda_n)_{n\ge1}$, nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_{\mathrm{in},n}(X)$ and $H_{\mathrm{out},n}(X)$, a density operator $\rho_n(X)$ on their ordered tensor product, and a finite assigned geometric value $S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[X]$ for each $n$. A **density operator** here is a self-adjoint endomorphism with nonnegative eigenvalues and trace one. The factor $H_{\mathrm{out},n}(X)$ represents the regulated bulk region $R_X$ and $H_{\mathrm{in},n}(X)$ its complementary factor; both factors and the state are supplied model data. Take $k_B>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Define $\rho_{\mathrm{out},n}(X)$ by tracing the first, $H_{\mathrm{in},n}(X)$, factor out of the ordered tensor product, using the finite partial-trace convention of the previously defined regulated entropy: in orthonormal bases $(e_i)$ and $(f_a)$ of the two factors, the $(a,b)$ entry is $\sum_i(\rho_n(X))_{(i,a),(i,b)}$. That convention proves the resulting endomorphism is a basis-independent density operator. With natural logarithms and $0\log0:=0$, set

$$S_{\mathrm{bulk},n}[R_X]:=-k_B\operatorname{tr}\!\left(\rho_{\mathrm{out},n}(X)\log\rho_{\mathrm{out},n}(X)\right),\qquad S_{\mathrm{gen},n}[X]:=S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[X]+S_{\mathrm{bulk},n}[R_X].$$

Require each $S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[X]$ to have units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$; its geometric terms, counterterms, and finite normalization are fixed model data in one declared regulator and renormalization scheme. On the optional Einstein–Hilbert area branch, the same fixed scheme also specifies, for each label $\Lambda_n$ and candidate, a dimensionless Borel function $0\le\chi_{\Lambda_n,X}\le1$ with compact support $K_{n,X}$ in $X^\circ:=X\setminus\partial X$. Put $h_X:=g|_{TX^\circ}$, a smooth positive-definite induced metric. Its density is $\mu_{h_X}=\sqrt{\det(h_{ab})}\,|dy^1\cdots dy^{d-1}|$ in a surface chart, as in [[def-riemannian-volume-density]]. The determinant transformation $h_y=J^Th_xJ$ gives the absolute-Jacobian density law. Under Countable Choice, meaning that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]), [[prop-riemannian-volume-is-the-radon-measure-of-the-riemannian-density]] supplies the corresponding compact-finite Borel measure $\operatorname{vol}_{h_X}$, independent of charts and orientation. Define the finite regulator-specific physical area by

$$\operatorname{Area}_{\Lambda_n}[X]:=\int_{X^\circ}\chi_{\Lambda_n,X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{h_X},\qquad 0\le\operatorname{Area}_{\Lambda_n}[X]\le\operatorname{vol}_{h_X}(K_{n,X})<\infty.$$

The bound follows directly from $0\le\chi\le1$ and compact finiteness. Smooth cutoffs give the usual intrinsic integral $\int\chi\mu_{h_X}$; sharp compact Borel cutoffs $\chi=\mathbf1_K$ are included. The measure domain here is the Borel domain, with no implicit completion. The geometric area has units $\mathrm{m^{d-1}}$ in the model's length convention. Countable Choice is carried precisely for this measure/integration interface, not for the chain algebra. With supplied $G_{\Lambda_n}>0$ of units $\mathrm{m^d\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$, this branch sets

$$S_{\mathrm{grav},n}[X]=\frac{k_Bc^3\operatorname{Area}_{\Lambda_n}[X]}{4G_{\Lambda_n}\hbar}+S_{\mathrm{other},n}[X],$$

where $c$ has units $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\hbar$ has units $\mathrm{J\,s}$, and the finite $S_{\mathrm{other},n}$ includes the scheme's specified counterterms and finite normalization. The cutoff functions, their relation to $\Lambda_n$, and every subtraction are fixed by that named scheme; no unregulated physical-metric area of a boundary-anchored surface is substituted. General assigned finite $S_{\mathrm{grav},n}$ data outside this optional area branch remain allowed.

Assign $S_{\mathrm{gen}}^{\mathrm{ren}}[X]$ exactly when the combined sequence $(S_{\mathrm{gen},n}[X])_{n\ge1}$ converges to a finite real number in that scheme, and then set it equal to that limit. No separate convergence of the two summands is required. If the combined sequence lacks a finite limit, no renormalized value is assigned.

For a smooth one-parameter family $X_\epsilon\in\mathcal X_A$ with fixed boundary anchor, fixed homology class, and $X_0=X$, let $V$ be its initial smooth normal velocity field, so $V_p\in(T_pX)^\perp_g$ for interior $p$, and the velocity extends to zero in $T\overline M$ along $\partial X$. When the derivative exists, define the first variation by $\delta_V S_{\mathrm{gen}}^{\mathrm{ren}}[X]:=\left.\frac{d}{d\epsilon}S_{\mathrm{gen}}^{\mathrm{ren}}[X_\epsilon]\right|_{\epsilon=0}$. Call $X$ **quantum stationary** when this derivative exists and is zero for every such allowed family. The term records the quantum bulk-entropy contribution to the functional; it does not assert a universal semiclassical or microscopic interpretation.

manifest_public_section.name: Postulate
manifest_public_section.expected: Fix an effective bulk model on a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ of dimension $d+1$, with $d\ge2$ and signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. Here AdS means anti-de Sitter. In this item, **asymptotically locally AdS** means that $M$ is the interior of a smooth manifold with boundary $\overline M$, and there is a dimensionless smooth defining function $z$ with $z>0$ on $M$, $z=0$ and $dz\ne0$ on $\partial\overline M$, such that $\overline g=z^2g$ extends smoothly to a nondegenerate metric whose induced boundary metric is Lorentzian. The model fixes its AdS length $L>0$ in metres, the asymptotic AdS boundary condition, bulk fields, semiclassical approximation, and conformal-boundary data; **semiclassical** here means that the bulk geometry is treated classically while the bulk entropy is computed from regulated quantum-state data on that geometry. No bulk field equation is inferred here.
manifest_public_section.replacement:
Fix an effective bulk model on a smooth, time-oriented Lorentzian spacetime $(M,g)$ of dimension $d+1$, with $d\ge2$ and signature $(-,+,\ldots,+)$. Here AdS means anti-de Sitter. In this item, **asymptotically locally AdS** means that $M$ is the interior of a smooth manifold with boundary $\overline M$, and there is a dimensionless smooth defining function $z$ with $z>0$ on $M$, $z=0$ and $dz\ne0$ on $\partial\overline M$, such that $\overline g=z^2g$ extends smoothly to a nondegenerate metric whose induced boundary metric is Lorentzian. The model fixes its AdS length $L>0$ in metres, the asymptotic AdS boundary condition, bulk fields, semiclassical approximation, and conformal-boundary data; **semiclassical** here means that the bulk geometry is treated classically while the bulk entropy is computed from regulated quantum-state data on that geometry. No bulk field equation is inferred here.

Choose a smooth spacelike boundary Cauchy slice $\mathcal C_{\partial}$ in the geometric inextendibility convention of [[def-tgrx-ads-regulated-generalized-entropy]]: increasing regular reparameterizations are allowed when testing extensions, and each maximal boundary causal curve meets it exactly once. Bulk candidate slices use that definition's boundary-inclusive Cauchy convention in $(\overline M,\overline g)$, with the compatible model-supplied time orientation; no interior-only Cauchy existence is inferred. Choose a relatively compact open region $A\subset\mathcal C_{\partial}$ with smooth boundary $\partial A$. The regulated boundary Hilbert space and its finite-dimensional subspace $\mathcal C_{\rm code}$ are model data; **regulated code subspace** means this specified finite-dimensional subspace, and every boundary density matrix in the chosen state family is supported on it. For a regulated boundary density matrix $\rho_{\partial}$, define its exact finite-cutoff entropy by $S_{\rm exact}(\rho_{\partial}):=-k_B\operatorname{tr}(\rho_{\partial}\log\rho_{\partial})$, using natural logarithms and $0\log0:=0$. A bulk candidate $X$ is admissible as in the regulated candidate-surface definition: it is a smooth embedded spacelike codimension-two surface with $\partial X=\partial A$, and its specified region $R_X$ represents the chosen homology class. A **quantum-stationary candidate** (also called a quantum extremal surface) is an admissible $X$ at which the first variation of the defined scheme-fixed generalized entropy exists and vanishes for every allowed smooth normal deformation that preserves the anchor and homology class. Let $\mathcal Q_A$ be the prescribed class of such candidates for the chosen boundary state. Use SI units: $k_B$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $c$ is in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and $\hbar$ is in $\mathrm{J\,s}$. Write $G_{\Lambda_n}>0$ for the model-supplied Newton coupling at regulator label $\Lambda_n$, in $\mathrm{m^d\,kg^{-1}\,s^{-2}}$ for this $(d+1)$-dimensional bulk. When the chosen Einstein–Hilbert branch uses the area term, use the same label-dependent physical-metric area $\operatorname{Area}_{\Lambda_n}[X]=\int_{X^\circ}\chi_{\Lambda_n,X}\,d\operatorname{vol}_{g|_{TX^\circ}}$ defined by the candidate-surface model, with its explicit Countable Choice integration premise and its fixed finite cutoff data. This term is $k_Bc^3\operatorname{Area}_{\Lambda_n}[X]/(4G_{\Lambda_n}\hbar)$, and all additional finite terms remain in the prescribed $S_{\mathrm{other},n}$. The cutoff area is in $\mathrm{m^{d-1}}$, so $[c^3\operatorname{Area}_{\Lambda_n}[X]]=\mathrm{m^{d+2}\,s^{-3}}=[G_{\Lambda_n}\hbar]$ and the factor multiplying $k_B$ is dimensionless. The metric, Borel cutoff, label dependence and subtraction convention are thus fixed before the combined renormalized limit is tested; an unregulated area at the conformal boundary is not asserted finite. For $d=3$ these are the usual four-dimensional SI units. Adopt

$$S_{\partial}^{\rm model}(A):=\min_{X\in\mathcal Q_A}S_{\rm gen}^{\rm ren}[X]$$

as the model's semiclassical boundary-entropy prediction only when $\mathcal Q_A$ is nonempty, the values are finite, and the minimum is attained. It does not identify this prediction with $S_{\rm exact}(\rho_{\partial})$. A **path-integral saddle** here is a stationary configuration of the chosen gravitational action; **saddle dominance** means that its contribution controls the specified path-integral approximation over competing configurations. Candidate existence, finite convergence, and dominance of the selected saddle are separate premises. The minimum rule is an adopted physical premise, not a consequence of the finite code entropy identity or the stationary Noether first law. It does not assert that the model describes nature, a universal RT/QES identity, or a continuum factorization of quantum fields.
